generic_sampling_rules.int_primary_key: assign sequential 1..N (offset past any compact keys) in table order before sampling any other column; never NULL; PKs are finalized before any foreign-key draw and never mutated afterwards; PK-formula checks are assertions only, never applied to random samples
generic_sampling_rules.int_foreign_key: copy an existing final parent key; child count per parent varies (some 0, some duplicated); never NULL unless column nullable
generic_sampling_rules.text_foreign_key: copy the final parent key rendered as str(); never NULL unless column nullable
generic_sampling_rules.int_quantity: integer in [0, 100000]; occasionally 0 and small values
generic_sampling_rules.short_enum_text: pick from column exception enum when listed, otherwise title-case word of 3-15 chars; allow near-duplicate variant with 10% share
generic_sampling_rules.short_label_text: distinct title-case phrase of 2-4 words; allow duplicates and near-variants
generic_sampling_rules.numeric_coercion: numeric columns (INT/REAL/NUMERIC) are always sampled by a numeric sampler; _apply_formulas coerces operands and skips/redraws non-numeric values before comparison; a single bad value never aborts an instance
generic_sampling_rules.exact_row_count: every table is finalized to exactly table_sizes_per_instance[t] generated rows after all transforms (PK dedup, group sizes, duplicates, ties, aggregate rebalance); transforms that drop rows refill to the target; compact rows are kept verbatim and counted separately
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: for every nullable column (schema NOT NULL flag false and not part of the PK) plant at least one NULL row per instance with a share following the compact DB (5% default); plant_nulls must run for every nullable column including phone_market.Num_of_stock; aggregate rebalance never overwrites planted NULLs; rules and formulas constrain only non-NULL operands

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: validity.invalid=20/20 with reasons no_rows_added=20, compact_rows_missing=20, new_integrity_failures=20; integrity.fk_violations=63. writer.write_instance_sqlite is called from cli._one as write_instance_sqlite(_G['schema'], inst, p) with no orig_path, so the compact database is never copied (the `if orig_path and os.path.exists(orig_path)` branch is skipped and only schema.ddl is executed). The generated rows are then appended to an empty database, so compact rows are missing and the FK targets (parent rows) do not exist, producing FK violations. This contradicts the module docstring ('Each instance is a copy of the compact database with the generated rows appended') and the specification's intent that compact rows are preserved.
issues.requested_revision: Pass the original database path through to write_instance_sqlite (e.g. add orig_path to the worker args and call write_instance_sqlite(schema, inst, p, orig_path)), so each unit is a copy of the compact DB with generated rows appended. Re-run and confirm validity.valid>0, compact_rows_missing=0, and fk_violations=0.

issues.evidence: instance.fill_foreign_keys_consistently: the branch `if rng.random() < 0.15: vals.append(rng.choice(pv)) else: vals.append(rng.choice(pv))` is identical in both branches, so the intended 'leave this parent without a child' behavior is not implemented. Combined with the missing compact rows, this means the unmatched_join_rows target (parent_rows_without_children=true) is not guaranteed by construction. Also, phone_market.Phone_ID is declared TEXT in the schema but the FK parent phone.Phone_ID is INT; fill_foreign_keys_consistently copies raw parent values without rendering them as text, which can produce type-mismatched joins and is inconsistent with the specification's 'text_foreign_key: copy parent key rendered as text'.
issues.requested_revision: Implement the unmatched-parent logic (e.g. deliberately exclude some parent keys from the child draw, or bias the draw so at least one parent has zero children), and render phone_market.Phone_ID values as text when copying from phone.Phone_ID. Verify with a query that at least one phone and one market row has no matching phone_market row.

issues.evidence: instance._apply_group_sizes sets vals[0]=vals[1]=vals[2]=vals[0] and vals[3]=vals[3], which forces a group of size >=3 but does not create groups of size 1 and 2 as required by the specification target 'group_sizes: 1, 2 and >= 3' for phone.Memory_in_G, phone.Phone_ID, phone.Name. Similarly _apply_ties only sets vals[1]=vals[0] (one tie) and _apply_duplicates overwrites the first n_dup entries with random existing values, which can destroy the group-size structure applied earlier (order of _apply_group_sizes then _apply_duplicates). The construction_pairs feedback shows separated=11/50, consistent with these patterns not being reliably realized.
issues.requested_revision: Rework _apply_group_sizes to explicitly produce at least one singleton group, one pair, and one group of size >=3 (e.g. assign distinct values to row 0, a repeated value to rows 1-2, and a third value to rows 3-5), and apply _apply_duplicates/_apply_ties in a way that does not overwrite the group-size structure (or re-apply group sizes after duplicates). Re-run and confirm the group-size targets are met.

issues.evidence: Specification semantic_rules_and_formulas lists Memory_in_G IN (16,32,64,128) and the comparison_boundary targets include -30,-29,-28,31,32,33,63,64,65. These are mutually inconsistent: the boundary values (e.g. -30, 31, 33, 65) violate the IN formula. The program resolves this by making _domain_for return the boundary domain for Memory_in_G (BOUNDARIES takes precedence over FORMULAS in _domain_for), so the IN formula is effectively not enforced, and _apply_formulas then rewrites any out-of-domain value back into (16,32,64,128), destroying the boundary values. The two rules cannot both hold.
issues.requested_revision: Reconcile the specification: either drop the Memory_in_G IN (16,32,64,128) formula (or widen it to include the boundary values), or restrict the comparison_boundary targets to values consistent with the formula. State which rule takes precedence so the program can implement it deterministically.

issues.evidence: instance._apply_aggregate_boundary distributes the target SUM over the generated phone_market rows only, ignoring the compact rows that (per the specification) are preserved. Once the compact-copy bug is fixed, the actual SUM(phone_market.Num_of_stock) will include compact rows and will not equal the target 1998..2001. Also _apply_aggregate_boundary runs after fill_foreign_keys_consistently and after sample_fresh_primary_keys/drop_unique_duplicates, so it can change Num_of_stock on rows that were already filtered, and it does not account for the number of rows actually kept.
issues.requested_revision: Compute the aggregate boundary against the total (compact + generated) rows, or document that the target applies to generated rows only and adjust the specification accordingly. Ensure the boundary is applied after row filtering so the final SUM matches the target.

issues.evidence: instance._apply_unmatched_parents is a no-op (`pass`), and _apply_different_values only bumps vals[1] if vals[0]==vals[1], which does not guarantee '>= 2 per group with different values' for phone.Price when the sampler already produced distinct values (fine) but also does not guarantee the scalar MAX query has >=2 qualifying rows in every group. The construction_pairs feedback (separated=11/50) suggests several patterns are not reliably realized.
issues.requested_revision: Implement _apply_unmatched_parents meaningfully (or remove it and rely on fill_foreign_keys_consistently), and strengthen _apply_different_values to guarantee at least two distinct Price values per relevant group. Re-run and confirm the corresponding construction pairs separate.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback reports fk_violations=39 and validity.invalid=13 with reason 'new_integrity_failures'. The generated instances violate foreign keys. Root cause is in instance.py: fill_foreign_keys_consistently() draws child FK values from the parent pool, but the parent pool is built from inst[pt][pc] BEFORE the parent table's own PK dedup/filtering (sample_fresh_primary_keys) and before _apply_group_sizes/_apply_duplicates/_apply_ties/_apply_formulas mutate parent columns. Specifically, _apply_group_sizes rewrites phone.Phone_ID values (rows 0..n) and _apply_formulas can rewrite phone.Phone_ID / market.Market_ID, so the FK values already drawn for phone_market no longer match any surviving parent key. Also, phone_market.Phone_ID is TEXT while phone.Phone_ID is INT; the FK is rendered as str(value) but the parent PK may be rewritten to a different integer after the child draw, leaving orphan text keys.
issues.requested_revision: Draw foreign-key child values AFTER all parent-table transformations (PK dedup, group-size, duplicates, ties, formulas) are finalized, or re-derive child FK values from the final parent key set. Ensure phone_market.Phone_ID text values are exactly str() of surviving phone.Phone_ID values. Re-run and confirm fk_violations=0 and validity.invalid=0.

issues.evidence: instance.py _apply_group_sizes is applied to phone.Phone_ID (a primary key) and rewrites vals[0..n] to base/base+1/base+2, which can collide with existing PK values and, more importantly, changes PKs after FK children were drawn. Similarly _apply_formulas includes ('phone','Phone_ID'):('>',0) and ('market','Market_ID'):('>',0) which can rewrite PKs post-FK-draw. This is the mechanism producing the FK violations above and also risks PK duplication (currently pk_duplicates=0 only by luck of the small sizes).
issues.requested_revision: Do not mutate primary-key columns after foreign keys have been generated. Either apply group-size/formula rules to PKs before FK generation and regenerate FKs from the final PK set, or exclude PK columns from post-hoc mutation and satisfy group-size targets via non-key columns where possible.

issues.evidence: Specification semantic_rules_and_formulas for phone.Memory_in_G states 'Memory_in_G IN (16,32,64,128) OR Memory_in_G IN (-30,-29,-28,31,33,63,65)' and the supporting_evidence admits 'boundary values conflict with the observed IN set and are admitted via the widened formula'. The atomic targets only require boundary probes around 32/64 (values -30..65); the plain IN set (16,32,64,128) is not evidenced by any atomic operation. issues.requested_revision: Mark the plain IN set (16,32,64,128) as uncertain/inferred rather than a supported rule, or drop it and keep only the boundary domain [-30,-29,-28,31,32,33,63,64,65] which is directly evidenced. issues.evidence: instance.py _apply_aggregate_boundary sets SUM(phone_market.Num_of_stock) over generated rows to a target in {1998,1999,2000,2001}. issues.evidence: Execution feedback: 14/20 units failed. 11 ValueError('PK formula failed for phone.Phone_ID value 0 > 0') / market.Market_ID value 0/-911984230 > 0, and 3 TypeError("'>=' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'int'"). The spec requires int_primary_key = 'sequential 1..N in table order; never NULL', but the program samples PKs through the generic NumberSampler (values.py make_column_sampler -> NumberSampler with scale=10, domain=None for Phone_ID/Market_ID since they are not in ENUMS/BOUNDARIES/FORMULAS-in). instance._apply_formulas then raises on any non-positive PK, aborting the unit. This is a construction error that blocks generation.
issues.requested_revision: Implement the spec's int_primary_key rule: assign sequential 1..N (offset past compact keys) to single-column integer PKs before any other column is sampled, and never route PK columns through the random NumberSampler. Keep the PK-formula check as an assertion only.

issues.evidence: TypeError("'>=' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'int'") in 3 units. _apply_formulas compares raw sampled values against numeric args (e.g. market.Num_of_shops >= 0, phone.Price >= 0, phone_market.Num_of_stock >= 0). NumberSampler._cast returns int/float, but StringSampler is selected for columns whose declared type is empty or 'blob' (values.make_column_sampler: `if t == '' or t == 'blob': return StringSampler(...)`), and the literal pool / original values can also inject strings. The formula loop does not coerce or skip non-numeric operands, so a string value crashes the unit.
issues.requested_revision: In _apply_formulas, coerce numeric operands (or skip/redraw non-numeric values for numeric columns) before comparison; ensure numeric columns are never sampled by StringSampler. Add a type guard so a single bad value cannot abort the whole instance.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback rows_added: market 7, phone_market 7, phone 5, but spec TABLE_SIZES = {'market': 6, 'phone': 5, 'phone_market': 6}. The extra rows come from the compact database being copied verbatim (writer.write_instance_sqlite copies orig_path) and then generated rows appended; the reported 'rows_added' counts only generated rows, yet market/phone_market show 7 > 6. This indicates the generated-row count is not exactly the specified size (likely because _finalize_table drops/keeps rows inconsistently, or the aggregate rebalance/group-size layout changes row counts). The spec says 'table_sizes_per_instance' are the generated rows per instance.
issues.requested_revision: Guarantee exactly TABLE_SIZES[t] generated rows per table after all finalisation (PK dedup, group-size, duplicates, ties, aggregate rebalance). If a transform must drop rows, refill to the target size; report generated-row counts separately from compact rows.

issues.evidence: Specification lists GROUP_SIZE_COLUMNS including ('phone','Phone_ID') with target '1, 2 and >= 3', but Phone_ID is the PRIMARY KEY, so groups of size >=2 are impossible without duplicating keys. The program silently skips PK columns in _apply_group_sizes (instance.py: `if (t, c) in pk_cols: continue`), and specification.py notes GROUP_SIZE_PRIMARY_KEYS = [('phone','Phone_ID')] 'satisfied structurally'. The atomic op GROUP(phone.phone_id) with group_sizes '1, 2 and >= 3' is therefore not actually satisfiable and is not implemented.
issues.requested_revision: Either drop ('phone','Phone_ID') from GROUP_SIZE_COLUMNS (it is a PK; group sizes 1/2/>=3 cannot hold) and record it as an unsupported pattern, or explicitly document that PK group-size targets are satisfied only by uniqueness. Do not list it as an applied group-size target.

issues.evidence: Specification FORMULAS includes ('phone','Memory_in_G'): ('in', (-30,-29,-28,31,32,33,63,64,65)) and BOUNDARIES the same set, while INFERRED_FORMULAS records the plain IN set (16,32,64,128). The atomic ops show comparison_boundary targets around 32/64 (values -30..65) but also 'set:PRED(phone.memory_in_g <> 64)', 'PRED(phone.memory_in_g <> 32)', 'PRED(phone.memory_in_g > -29)'. The boundary domain is evidenced, but the spec's claim that the plain IN set is 'inferred and not supported' is a design decision, not a database fact; the boundary values -30/-29/-28 are far outside any plausible memory size and are only boundary probes. This is acceptable as a design choice but should be flagged as uncertain rather than presented as the only supported domain.
issues.requested_revision: Keep the boundary domain but mark Memory_in_G domain as 'boundary-probe only, uncertain' in the specification, and ensure the sampler can also produce the plain IN set (16,32,64,128) as a secondary domain so value variation around the real memory sizes remains possible. Do not present the boundary set as the sole evidenced domain.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: 6 of 20 instances failed with TypeError("'>=' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'int'") (units 4, 11, 15, 16, 18, 19). The specification's supporting_evidence claims numeric_coercion 'fixes 3 TypeError failures', but the run still produces 6. The failure is in _apply_formulas: for op '>=' the code computes `cv = _coerce_like(v, arg) if op in ('>', '>=') else v`, but _coerce_like only coerces when `arg` is a tuple of numbers; for scalar numeric args (e.g. ('>=', 0) on phone.Price, market.Num_of_employees, market.Num_of_shops, market.Ranking, phone_market.Num_of_stock) it returns v unchanged, so a string value reaches `cv >= arg` and raises TypeError. This is a real bug, not a sampling artifact: the same code path is hit whenever a numeric column's sampler yields a string (e.g. via StringSampler fallback for a column whose declared type is empty/blob, or via _refill_table appending values from a sampler that produced strings).
issues.requested_revision: Fix _coerce_like (or _apply_formulas) so that scalar numeric formula arguments also trigger _coerce_numeric on the operand, and re-draw/skip non-coercible values as the spec's numeric_coercion rule states. Re-run and confirm n_fail == 0.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: rows_skipped = {phone_market: 54} while rows_added = {phone_market: 30}. The writer reports 54 generated phone_market rows that failed to insert (PK/unique collisions on (Market_ID, Phone_ID) after FK draw, or NOT NULL/type issues). The spec's exact_row_count rule requires every table to be finalised to exactly TABLE_SIZES[t] generated rows; phone_market is finalised to 6 per instance but only ~2.1/instance survive insertion. The _finalize_table for phone_market runs choose_compact_aware_pks/sample_fresh_primary_keys BEFORE the FK columns are populated (FKs are drawn in build_random_instance before _finalize_table, but the PK tuple for phone_market is (Market_ID, Phone_ID) — both FK columns — so dedup on the composite key is not effective against the random FK draw, and _refill_table skips FK columns entirely, so refill cannot restore the count).
issues.requested_revision: For tables whose PK is composed of FK columns (phone_market), deduplicate the composite (Market_ID, Phone_ID) tuple after the FK draw and refill to the target size by re-drawing FK pairs (not by skipping FK columns in _refill_table). Verify rows_skipped[phone_market] == 0 and rows_added[phone_market] == 6 * n_ok.

issues.evidence: Specification: phone.Memory_in_G formula is `IN (-30,-29,-28,31,32,33,63,64,65,16,128)` but the secondary domain MEMORY_SECONDARY is [16,32,64,128] and MEMORY_SECONDARY_SHARE=0.30. The formula's IN set omits 32 and 64 (it lists 16 and 128 but not 32/64), while the boundary set includes 31,32,33,63,64,65. This is internally inconsistent: a value of 32 or 64 drawn from the secondary domain would fail the formula and be re-drawn, so the secondary domain is effectively [16,128] only. The spec's own note says 'plain IN set (16,32,64,128) kept as secondary domain', contradicting the FORMULAS entry.
issues.requested_revision: Make the FORMULAS IN set for phone.Memory_in_G consistent with the union of BOUNDARIES and MEMORY_SECONDARY (i.e. include 32 and 64), or remove 32/64 from MEMORY_SECONDARY. Document which is intended.

issues.evidence: Specification: group_sizes target for phone.Memory_in_G is '1, 2 and >= 3', but execution feedback shows group_sizes for phone.Memory_in_G as [1,1,3], [1,2,2], [1,1,1,2], [1,1,1,1,1] — i.e. many instances lack a group of size >= 3 (e.g. [1,2,2] has max size 2; [1,1,1,2] has max size 2). The _apply_group_sizes layout (row0=A, rows1-2=B, rows3-5=C) is applied, but subsequent _apply_formulas re-draws values (e.g. 32/64 not in the IN set) and _refill_table appends rows, breaking the layout. The spec claims group_sizes is 'applied by construction' but the execution evidence shows it is not reliably satisfied.
issues.requested_revision: Either (a) apply group_sizes AFTER formulas and refill, or (b) make the formula domain compatible with the group-size layout so re-draws do not destroy it. Confirm every instance has a group of size >= 3 for phone.Memory_in_G and phone.Name.
